components.css: .ds-cartella { width: 432px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgb(196 30 42 / 0.28); border-radius: 16px; overflow: hidden; font-family: Bricolage Grotesque, sans-serif; } .ds-cartella-strip { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 8px 16px; background: #c41e2a; color: #fff; font-size: 12px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-cartella-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(9, 1fr); } .ds-numero { position: relative; display: grid; place-content: center; aspect-ratio: 1; isolation: isolate; color: #a31621; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; border-right: 1px solid rgb(196 30 42 / 0.28); cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.3s ease-out; } .ds-numero:last-child { border-right: none; } .ds-numero:not(.ds-blank):hover { background: rgb(196 30 42 / 0.05); } .ds-numero::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; width: min(100%, 2.4em); aspect-ratio: 1; translate: -50% -50%; border-radius: 9999px; background: #d6ad78; border: 1.5px solid #a97a45; box-shadow: 0 2px 4px -1px rgb(60 35 10 / 0.35); z-index: -1; scale: 0; transition: scale 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-numero.ds-on { color: #84151e; } .ds-numero.ds-on::before { scale: 1; } .ds-blank { cursor: default; background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, rgb(196 30 42 / 0.1) 0 1px, transparent 1px 7px); }

narrative.overview:
Ambo! is quiet contemporary product UI wrapped around two objects taken straight from the family tombola: the paper cartella printed in red, and the round beech numeretto pulled from the bag. Those two objects are the entire theme. Everything else (header, forms, prize split, footer) is plain, neutral and hairline-thin so the numbers can be read from across a room.

The palette is a single brand red on warm neutral grey, plus one material: flat beech wood. Red is ink (numerals, grid lines, the hatch of empty cells, the header bar, primary actions); beech is the token that lands on a drawn or marked number. There is no faked grain, no folk ornament and no texture beyond the faint diagonal hatch of a blank cell. Density is calm: generous gaps, one panel per job, Bricolage Grotesque throughout with semibold tabular numerals.

The world explicitly rejects the folk-costume tombola (the earlier carretto direction, turned down as dated) and the generic neon bingo app.
keyCharacteristics: One brand red (#c41e2a family) used as print, never as fill for large surfaces beyond the slim header bar and card headers.
Drawn and marked numbers become flat beech tokens with a darker beech edge and a soft cast shadow, carrying a deep red numeral.
Neutral warm-grey ground with white or near-black panels, 1px hairlines and 16px corners.
Bricolage Grotesque only; numerals are semibold and tabular everywhere.
Light and dark themes share the same structure; dark lifts the print to a softer red.

rules.name: The Ink, Not Paint Rule
rules.body: Red is printed: numerals, grid lines, hatch, a slim bar. It never floods a panel or a page section.

rules.name: The Wood Means Drawn Rule
rules.body: Beech appears only on a number that has been drawn or marked. A wooden surface anywhere else breaks the game's own signal.

rules.name: The Tabular Numeral Rule
rules.body: Every number (cells, tokens, counts, game ID, prize amounts) is set with tabular figures so columns and counts never jitter.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque only. Emphasis is weight (500/600) and the red, not a display face or letterspaced caps.

rules.name: The Only Objects Cast Rule
rules.body: Only wooden tokens and their dish carry shadows. UI panels, buttons and inputs stay flat.

dos: **Do** use red only as print and as small solid accents (header bar, primary button, progress, card strip).
**Do** show every drawn or marked number as a beech token with the darker beech edge and a token-ink numeral.
**Do** set every numeral in Bricolage Grotesque semibold with tabular figures.
**Do** separate surfaces with 1px hairlines and 16px panel corners; switch to the red print line for grids.
**Do** honour reduced motion: tokens fade instead of rolling or scaling.
donts: **Don't** add folk ornament, carretto motifs, painted borders or faked wood grain; the beech is flat colour.
**Don't** put shadows on panels, buttons or inputs; shadow is reserved for wooden objects.
**Don't** use beech for anything other than a drawn or marked number (the logo is the one approved exception).
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or letterspaced uppercase labels.
